prereq_check.title: Checking your Mac
prereq_check.subtitle: macOS, Apple Silicon, RAM, disk
prereq_check.why: Ostler runs entirely on this machine. We confirm it has the muscle for local AI before we touch anything.

setup_questions.title: A few questions
setup_questions.subtitle: About two minutes; setup keeps going on its own afterwards
setup_questions.why: Your name, your country, your timezone, your assistant's name. These shape everything Ostler does later, but you only answer them once.

setup_complete_wrap_up.title: Questions done. Setup continues in the background.
setup_complete_wrap_up.subtitle: Roughly 45 minutes to a few hours; it runs on its own
setup_complete_wrap_up.why: Your answers are saved. The install now runs unattended for roughly 45 minutes to a few hours, depending on how much history is on your Mac and how fast your connection is: Docker, Ollama, the knowledge graph, the assistant binary. Long quiet stretches are normal while things download and set up. You can leave it running and check back later. Nothing else needs your input.

homebrew_install.title: Installing Homebrew + system tools
homebrew_install.subtitle: The package layer Ostler uses
homebrew_install.why: Homebrew is the standard macOS package manager. Ostler uses it to fetch Docker, Ollama, and a few CLI tools. Nothing system-wide that conflicts with what you already have.
homebrew_install.long_running_copy: First-time Homebrew install can take a few minutes on slow networks.

docker_install.title: Starting Docker
docker_install.subtitle: Container runtime for the data pipeline
docker_install.why: Ostler runs its databases (Qdrant, Oxigraph, Redis) and wiki in Docker. Ollama and the assistant binary run natively – Docker is only the data layer.

reboot_selfheal.title: Restart recovery
reboot_selfheal.subtitle: Optional, and off unless you say otherwise
reboot_selfheal.why: Ostler's services start when you sign in, so after a power-cut this Mac sits at the login screen and Ostler stays dark until someone signs in. Ostler can offer to change that by storing your login password on this Mac so it signs itself in on its own. The password is stored scrambled rather than encrypted, and anyone with an administrator account here, or with the disk in their hands, can read it back, so the question defaults to no. It is only offered when FileVault is off, because FileVault stops automatic sign-in. Say no and nothing is stored and nothing changes.

ollama_install.title: Setting up Ollama
ollama_install.subtitle: Local AI engine (no cloud)
ollama_install.why: Ollama runs language models on your Mac's Apple Silicon. Every prompt your assistant answers, every wiki summary, runs through this. Nothing leaves the machine.

config_save.title: Saving your configuration
config_save.subtitle: Names, timezone, channel choices
config_save.why: Writes your answers to ~/.ostler/config/ so future runs (and the assistant) pick them up without asking again.

encrypt_db.title: Securing your databases
encrypt_db.subtitle: Passphrase + SQLCipher
encrypt_db.why: A passphrase you choose encrypts Ostler's sensitive databases with SQLCipher, and a recovery key is generated and stored securely on this Mac in case you forget it. You'll type the passphrase each time you start the Hub UI. For full at-rest protection of everything on your Mac, keep macOS FileVault turned on.

fda_extract.title: Reading your Mac's databases
fda_extract.subtitle: The instant onboarding bit
fda_extract.why: macOS won't let any app read your messages, mail, notes, calendars or photos without your explicit say-so. We need that one permission so Ostler can pull all of it together into your knowledge graph. Everything stays on this Mac – nothing is sent anywhere. You'll grant it once in System Settings and macOS remembers from then on.
fda_extract.long_running_copy: First-run extraction can take a couple of minutes if your Mail or Photos library is large.

graph_db_start.title: Starting the knowledge graph
graph_db_start.subtitle: Qdrant + Oxigraph + Redis
graph_db_start.why: Three small databases boot up: vectors for semantic search, RDF triples for relationships, Redis for the message bus. All local, all yours.

vane_install.title: Starting local web search
vane_install.subtitle: Vane container (bundles SearXNG)
vane_install.why: Vane is the local web-search front end. It runs in a container on your Mac and talks to your local Ollama – web searches never leave your machine. If the container fails to start, the rest of Ostler keeps working; you can retry web search later.
vane_install.long_running_copy: First-time pull is ~3.6 GB (SearXNG bundled in). Subsequent starts are seconds.

ai_models.title: Downloading AI models
ai_models.subtitle: This is the big one (~7GB)
ai_models.why: The assistant model and the embedding model. One large download, then nothing more from the cloud. If your connection drops we retry three times.
ai_models.long_running_copy: On a slow connection this can take 15-20 minutes. You can leave the installer running.

import_pipeline.title: Installing the data import pipeline
import_pipeline.subtitle: Parsers for 20+ platforms
import_pipeline.why: The pipeline parses the data sources you've consented to: GDPR exports, Apple Mail, iCloud calendars, browser history. Each parser is local Python, no cloud.

gws_install.title: Calendar / Gmail bridge
gws_install.subtitle: Google Workspace CLI + iCloud wrapper
gws_install.why: Ostler talks to your Gmail and Google Calendar via Google's own Workspace CLI (gws) running locally on this Mac, and to iCloud over CalDAV with an app-specific password. Nothing leaves the machine; OAuth happens between the CLI and Google.

import_data.title: Importing your data
import_data.subtitle: Building your knowledge graph
import_data.why: First-pass import: contacts, conversations, calendar events, Safari history. The wiki compiler runs after this, turning the graph into pages you can read.
import_data.long_running_copy: Import time scales with your history. Years of iMessage data can take 10-20 minutes.

doctor_setup.title: Setting up Ostler Doctor
doctor_setup.subtitle: Diagnostic dashboard
doctor_setup.why: Doctor is the local-only health dashboard. If something stops working, Doctor tells you what and why. No telemetry, no cloud – diagnostics stay on your Mac.

knowledge_setup.title: Setting up the Knowledge service
knowledge_setup.subtitle: Evernote import
knowledge_setup.why: Installs the ostler-knowledge CLI under ~/.ostler/services/knowledge/. Lets you import an Evernote export into your local graph later from the Doctor dashboard. Your notes and images stay on your Mac.

hub_power.title: Hub power policy
hub_power.subtitle: MacBook battery-aware mode
hub_power.why: On a MacBook Hub, Docker and Ollama pause when you unplug and resume when you plug in, so your battery life stays roughly normal. On a Mac Mini, this is a no-op.

email_ingest.title: Email ingest
email_ingest.subtitle: Hourly Apple Mail drain
email_ingest.why: Once an hour, Ostler drains new mail from Apple Mail's local store into the graph. Apple does the auth (IMAP/OAuth), Ostler reads the local copy. Zero credentials held by us.

whatsapp_bundle.title: WhatsApp conversations
whatsapp_bundle.subtitle: Conversation memory
whatsapp_bundle.why: Every fifteen minutes, Ostler reads recent WhatsApp conversations your Mac has synced (about the last year) and turns each into a short summary, any to-dos, a clean transcript, and metadata. Everything stays on your Mac; nothing is sent to us.

email_bundle.title: Email conversations
email_bundle.subtitle: Conversation memory
email_bundle.why: Ostler turns your recent email threads (from Apple Mail's local store) into short summaries, to-dos, clean transcripts and metadata, so you can search and reference them. Everything stays on your Mac; nothing is sent to us.

spoken_bundle.title: Meeting and voice conversations
spoken_bundle.subtitle: Conversation memory
spoken_bundle.why: Ostler turns your own recorded meetings and voice notes into short summaries, to-dos, clean transcripts and metadata. These are your own recordings, consented when you captured them. Everything stays on your Mac.

imessage_bundle.title: iMessage conversations
imessage_bundle.subtitle: Conversation memory
imessage_bundle.why: Ostler turns your recent iMessage conversations (from this Mac's Messages store) into short summaries, to-dos, clean transcripts and metadata, so you can search and reference them. Everything stays on your Mac; nothing is sent to us.

wiki_recompile_agent.title: Wiki rebuild scheduler
wiki_recompile_agent.subtitle: Daily knowledge compilation
wiki_recompile_agent.why: Once a day (default 4am) the wiki compiler reruns over fresh data. Karpathy-style: facts in, knowledge out. You can also trigger it on demand later.

ostler_assistant.title: Installing the assistant
ostler_assistant.subtitle: Your local AI agent
ostler_assistant.why: The Rust binary that drives iMessage, email, and tool use. Lives at ~/.ostler/bin and runs as a launchd agent. Everything it can do is gated by the channels and permissions you set.

wiki_compile.title: Compiling your wiki
wiki_compile.subtitle: First-run knowledge build
wiki_compile.why: Turns the imported graph into a browsable wiki at localhost:8044. Pages: people, places, organisations, threads, topics. Each one is a flat MkDocs page you can also edit by hand.
wiki_compile.long_running_copy: First compile crunches everything from scratch. Subsequent runs are incremental and much faster.

health_check.title: Health check
health_check.subtitle: Confirming everything is up
health_check.why: Quick sanity pass – every container running, every LaunchAgent loaded, the wiki responding. If anything is off, the report tells you exactly what.

initial_hydrate.title: Loading your data into Ostler
initial_hydrate.subtitle: The first pass over everything you just connected
initial_hydrate.why: Ostler now walks everything you gave it access to and turns it into your knowledge graph: who you know, what you have talked about, where you have been. This is the longest single stretch of the install and it runs entirely on this Mac. Nothing is uploaded.
initial_hydrate.long_running_copy: This scales with your history. A Mac with years of mail and messages can sit here for a long while. It is working, not stuck.

hydrate_graph.title: Hydrating your graph from iCloud
hydrate_graph.subtitle: Contacts, calendars and reminders
hydrate_graph.why: Your iCloud contacts, calendars and reminders are read straight off this Mac and folded into the graph, so the assistant knows who your people are before you ask it anything. This is a local read. Nothing is fetched from Apple and nothing is sent to us.
hydrate_graph.long_running_copy: Large address books and long calendar histories take a few minutes.

hydrate_imessage.title: Hydrating iMessage contacts
hydrate_imessage.subtitle: Who you actually talk to
hydrate_imessage.why: Ostler reads your local Messages database to work out who you speak to and how often, which is what lets it tell an old colleague from your sister. The conversations stay on this Mac.
hydrate_imessage.long_running_copy: Years of message history take a few minutes to walk.

hydrate_browsing.title: Hydrating your browsing history
hydrate_browsing.subtitle: Interests, from your own browser
hydrate_browsing.why: Safari and Chrome history is read locally to learn what you are interested in, so recommendations are about you rather than about averages. If you would rather it did not, you can turn browsing capture off later in Preferences.

hydrate_email_preferences.title: Loading your email preferences
hydrate_email_preferences.subtitle: How you use your inbox
hydrate_email_preferences.why: Ostler looks at how you handle mail: who you reply to quickly, what you archive unread, which senders matter. That is what later lets it triage for you instead of just listing things.

hydrate_apple_notes.title: Reading your Apple Notes
hydrate_apple_notes.subtitle: Your own written notes
hydrate_apple_notes.why: Apple Notes often holds the things nothing else does: lists, drafts, half-finished thoughts. Ostler reads them locally so they are searchable alongside everything else.

hydrate_people.title: Indexing your people for search
hydrate_people.subtitle: Making everyone findable
hydrate_people.why: Every person Ostler has found is indexed so you can search by name, by company, or by how you know them. This is the step that makes the People tab useful rather than a list.
hydrate_people.long_running_copy: Indexing scales with how many people were found.

cm048_setup.title: Setting up conversation memory
cm048_setup.subtitle: So it remembers what you said
cm048_setup.why: This is the piece that lets the assistant carry context between conversations rather than starting cold every time. It runs locally against your own model.

cm019_setup.title: Setting up preference enrichment
cm019_setup.subtitle: Turning history into preferences
cm019_setup.why: Preference enrichment is what turns raw history into something useful: not just that you went somewhere, but that you liked it. It runs in the background after the install and keeps improving.

ical_server_setup.title: Setting up your calendar and contacts service
ical_server_setup.subtitle: The local service the assistant asks
ical_server_setup.why: A small service runs on this Mac and answers questions about your calendar, contacts and email on the assistant's behalf. It listens on this machine only.

imessage_bridge.title: Tidying up an old messaging helper
imessage_bridge.subtitle: Housekeeping from an earlier design
imessage_bridge.why: Ostler used to need a separate helper to read Messages across two machines. It runs on one Mac now, so this step switches that helper off. Nothing you set up is lost.

wiki_recompile_catchup_agent.title: Scheduling your first-day catch-up
wiki_recompile_catchup_agent.subtitle: Your wiki keeps building after this finishes
wiki_recompile_catchup_agent.why: Your personal wiki is not finished when the installer is. This schedules a catch-up pass that keeps compiling pages over your first day, so the wiki fills out while you get on with things.

editor_frontpage.title: Setting up your Front Page
editor_frontpage.subtitle: Refreshed every hour
editor_frontpage.why: The Front Page is what Ostler thinks you should see right now: what is coming up, who you owe a reply, what changed. It rebuilds itself every hour from your own graph.

ostler_remotecapture.title: Setting up call and meeting transcripts
ostler_remotecapture.subtitle: Recording is always your choice
ostler_remotecapture.why: This installs the app that can record and transcribe your calls and meetings on this Mac. It records nothing until you explicitly start it, and transcription happens locally.

ostler_hub_app.title: Setting up the Ostler app
ostler_hub_app.subtitle: The window you will actually use
ostler_hub_app.why: This is the desktop app: your wiki, your people, your timeline and the chat. It lives in the menu bar and opens on this Mac.

tailscale_connect.title: Connect your iPhone and Watch
tailscale_connect.subtitle: One QR code, on your phone
tailscale_connect.why: Scan the code with the Ostler iOS app to link your phone to this Mac. The connection is private between your own devices. You can skip this and pair later from the app.
tailscale_connect.long_running_copy: This step waits for you. Nothing is timing out.
